record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: Which experimentally testable predictions of the Brightsen nucleon cluster model are correct, including its claims about prompt-neutron yields in fission, low-energy nuclear transformations, antimatter and 'unmatter' entities inside nuclei, antigravity signatures of antimatter, induced transmutation of radioactive nuclei, helium-4 sub-cluster structure, new intranuclear force effects, a magic number at N = 172, Z = 106, A = 278, and a specific cluster-based explanation of the large neutron cross section of boron-10?

evidence.quote: Presented in this section are a number of unsolved problems, questions, and future experimental pathways based on the Brightsen Nucleon Cluster Model formalism

If experimentally confirmed, then predictive equations will need to be developed using the Brightsen Model formalism of union of matter and antimatter clusters (e.g., the unsolved mathematical formation of unmatter entities inside nuclei).
The Brightsen Model predicts that the next ‘magic number’ will be found at N = 172, Z = 106, A = 278 (Seaborgium-278).

artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that the Brightsen Nucleon Cluster Model's predictions remain unverified experimentally. Follow-up notes (e.g. the 2010 APS abstract "Some Unsolved Problems, Questions, and Applications of the Brightsen Nucleon Cluster Model") still list these predictions as open, and the model is described as not widely accepted, with no published experimental confirmation of items such as the N=172, Z=106 magic number, unmatter entities, antigravity signatures, or the ⁴He sub-cluster structure. No superheavy magic nucleus at A=278 Sg has been observed, and unmatter/antimatter-in-nuclei claims have not been experimentally established. The questions therefore appear to remain open.
